note: The check suite runs ONLY checks registered here (founding spec §4).
Registration requires an admission record: the named defect the check
caught or the contract it uniquely carries, the licensing issue, and a
removal signal declared at birth. An unregistered check file is dead
code; one meta check asserts the registry and the checks/ tree agree.
Every removal signal names its observing instrument (kogaki#113):
removal_instrument is `act: <the act that already happens and owes the
removal row>`, `none: <why no act in this repository can observe it>`,
condition now holds; exit 1 = not yet; anything else = the probe could
not establish). Probes are evaluated by check-registry-conformance.sh,
which renders candidates report-only — removal stays a judgment.

admission.contract: registry/tree agreement, both ways (an unregistered check file is dead code, a registered file that does not exist is a dangling entry), plus admission-shape validation: every registered entry carries a non-empty admission record — the contracts this file's own note declares and nothing else carries
admission.removal_signal: a suite runner whose discovery is registry-driven, making an unregistered file unrunnable by construction — constrain-generation subsumes this detection
admission.removal_instrument: act: the PR that moves discovery-refusal and admission-shape validation into the runner itself — its licensing issue owes this check's removal row; today's runner iterates registered entries but neither refuses unregistered files nor validates admission shape, so the signal's condition is a judgment over what the runner enforces, not a tree fact

admission.contract: the consult-first discipline's reading act: reports the branch's consulted: receipt count and distinct pins, rendering zero explicitly — an obligation generates no event to hook, so observability is the whole remedy. Fails only on a malformed receipt, never on the count. Fenced-block quotations are MENTIONS of the grammar, not receipts, and are excluded from the counted set (kogaki#41, the PR #40 false positive). Parses the v2 continuation block (kogaki#28, story 1.10) — request_id, outcome, one query line per framing, indented under line one, all OPTIONAL so every v1 receipt in git history stays valid — and widens malformed to FIVE field defects, all conformance rather than counting: an outcome outside the hub's ratified triple (a bare `miss` collapses the two causes the 2026-08-02 correction separated), a re-framed outcome recording fewer than every framing's query, an `uncovered-after-N` whose N disagrees with the number of query lines recorded (shape validation alone let a receipt claim seven framings while recording two), an N below the two-framing floor (a miss is not recordable as uncovered until re-asked along another axis; the floor is stated as its own clause because it is currently also implied by the query rule, and an implied invariant is one a refactor drops unnoticed), and a PARTIAL v2 receipt — continuations stay optional so a v1 receipt is valid, but once ANY continuation is present the receipt owes all three fields SPEC §4 requires (PR #43 review). The embedded fixture pass is the discrimination evidence, run every invocation, and asserts the PARSED FIELDS rather than only counts — a count-only assertion cannot observe whether the continuation fields were read at all, which measured 2 of 8 v2 cases discriminating before the assertion was widened and 6 of 8 after. States what it does NOT verify: the query-count rule is satisfied by two rephrasings of one question, and axis-variation is a judgment no count can observe — the check asserts the framings were RECORDED and routes whether they differed to the review lane, with a receipt found carrying two rephrasings as the observation that would earn a real detector. Empty values are handled by ONE rule applied in the parse: continuation PRESENCE is recorded as a fact about the text rather than inferred from value truthiness, and an empty value is absent for every field alike — before which empty query lines counted as recorded framings, so `uncovered-after-3-framings` with three blank queries satisfied N == len() (PR #43 re-review)
admission.license: kogaki#7 (story 1.3); use-mention exclusion kogaki#41; v2 continuation block kogaki#28 (story 1.10)
admission.removal_signal: a gateway-side consumer receipt surface that reports served consultations back to the consumer — that would verify against the server's record rather than the consumer's claim, superseding this check's weaker evidence
admission.removal_instrument: none: the superseding carrier would land in tsurezure-gateway, and no act in this repository can observe another repository's surface appearing — the cross-repo hold class product-lab#158 documented

admission.contract: the client kit's install guarantees, fired rather than merely written: fresh-install layout, idempotency, the one-line degrade at exit 11, the pinless-body deny, harness-loadable skill frontmatter, the entry-2 boundary (no kit tool reads gateway state), and the absence of any colocation default. Also the transport's RECEIPT MODE (kogaki#66, story 1.20), where the emitter replaces hand transcription: the refusal to assign the `outcome` token — `deferred-slot: consult-outcome-token-assignment` is open, so a default would be code embedding an undecided choice and the refusal must name the slot rather than read as a syntax error; that a degraded run emits NO receipt block, because a receipt for a consult that did not happen is the fabrication the clause exists to prevent; that receipt mode is opt-in, so the pre-1.20 invocation is byte-for-byte unchanged; that the marked-exception key is the fixed UNINDENTED `consult-receipt:` token, which is correctness rather than style because check-consult-receipts.sh recognises only request_id/outcome/query as continuation keys and an unrecognised indented key above them ends the continuation scan, leaving a field-less v1 line that silently passes; and the emitter's own 13-case composition fixture pass, which asserts line one is COPIED from the served response rather than re-derived, one query line per framing actually run, pins merged under one commit, the token carried untouched, and five refusals where the wire did not carry what a receipt asserts. Registered because a test nothing invokes is the orphan-guard shape kogaki#6 was filed to end
admission.removal_signal: the kit's separation into its own repository (fires on a second installing consumer, per kogaki#9) — the test goes with it and this repo stops being its home
admission.removal_instrument: act: the admission gate of a second installing consumer (the trigger kogaki#9 names) — the sitting that admits consumer two owes the kit's move and this check's removal row in the same act

admission.contract: the owner-facing proposal contract as a record shape (manifest item 3, specs/SPEC.md:97-98): Where/Why with the computed premise's negation offered as a first-class option, machine-proposed options plus an UNCONDITIONAL free-text override, payload capture (options offered + answer, never the answer alone), and the non-member fallback of specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md:76-86 — an act in neither the navigation nor the proposal list is a report, never a silent classification. Carries the effect-stating property's FORM floor only and says so in its own output; sufficiency is judgment and routes to kogaki#13
admission.removal_signal: a second consumer whose proposals differ in shape from Terrain's — the record schema was specced against one implementation, so a second one is the evaluation of the shape, not a widening of it: either the schema generalizes (and this check moves to it) or the contract splits per consumer and this file, which validates a single shape, is the wrong carrier
admission.removal_instrument: act: the admission gate of a second proposal-emitting consumer — the sitting that admits it evaluates whether the record schema generalizes, and owes this check's re-siting or split in the same act

admission.contract: the gate carrier (manifest item 4, specs/SPEC.md:99-101): the declared gate registry as the enumeration a coverage claim is a fraction OF, the MEDIUM BINDING (a Claude Code host renders a gate through the selector affordance and never prose — the one form of the legibility rule that is falsifiable), AskUserQuestion tool-use evidence beside every captured answer, payload/answer capture including the GATE-LESS row no suite upstream held, and the machine's own comparison (ranked recommendation, per-option evidence, overturning evidence, no pre-selection) sited here rather than in item 3. Its reporting carries the three-part crash remedy: guarded rows, CANNOT-DETERMINE rendered separately from FAIL so a crash is never spent as a positive finding, and repetition disclosed as one deterministic cause rather than N confirmations. Shares no machinery with check-proposal-contract.sh, which binds a record and by its own decision delivers no rendering. Carries the comparison's STRUCTURE only and says so in its own output; whether the evidence is the evidence bearing on an option, and whether a gate reads as a gate beyond its named affordance, are judgment and route to kogaki#13
admission.removal_signal: a harness-side carrier that enforces the medium binding at the moment a gate is raised — a Stop or PostToolUse hook reading AskUserQuestion tool-use evidence directly (topics/claude-code-ops.md:35@5f769dfe names the transcript/tool-call layer as never exercised). That would verify against the host's own record rather than against a declared registry and a committed capture file, and constrain-generation subsumes after-the-fact detection: this check goes when it lands
admission.removal_instrument: act: the PR that lands the harness-side medium-binding hook — its licensing issue owes this check's removal row in the same act, so the fired trigger is observed at the act that fires it

admission.contract: Terrain's three ported contracts over every survey record in the tree (manifest item 1, specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md §2): completeness as a cover counted in placements — every Strand placed, no-relation Strands in an explicit named section, nothing silently dropped; the figure counted AFTER composition, recomputed here from the placements themselves, naming which family it counted; and navigation state carrying no narrowing key, so a survey record cannot smuggle the refused minimal-form bundling in as a field — plus the seam pin on every record. The detection half behind terrain/terrain.mjs's generation-time refusal (validateSurvey applies the same schema-carried rules before writing); the fixture pass is the evidence both halves discriminate. Carries composition FACTS only and says so in its own output; whether the grouping axis serves the owner and whether a ratified narrowing was worth taking are judgment and route to kogaki#13
admission.removal_signal: terrain/terrain.mjs validateSurvey becoming the registry-verified SOLE writer of survey records, with the fixture pass exercising the mjs validator directly rather than this mirror — once no unvalidated write path exists, constrain-generation subsumes after-the-fact detection, the same shape the registry meta-check's own removal signal ratified (kogaki#2)
admission.removal_instrument: act: the PR that makes terrain/terrain.mjs validateSurvey the sole write path — sole-writer-ness is a judgment over write paths, not a tree probe, and that PR's licensing issue owes the removal row

admission.contract: the boundary-receipt binding at the merge layer (specs/SPEC.md §4, kogaki#25): a consultation-map boundary whose trigger terms MATCH the branch, with ZERO receipts present, FAILS — which is what converts the map from advice an agent may remember into a carrier that binds on every PR. A PRESENCE CHECK OVER TWO DECLARED ENUMERATIONS (the map's entries, the branch's receipts), both named in the output because a coverage claim is a fraction OF an enumeration. It NEVER BRANCHES ON THE OUTCOME TOKEN and structurally cannot: it reads line one only, so `discriminating`, `covered-after-reframing` and `uncovered-after-N-framings` satisfy it alike — the obligation is TO ASK and never TO HAVE FOUND (as corrected for kogaki#32), and a check that passed on some outcomes and failed on others would be judging whether the consultation SUCCEEDED, which is the review lane's property. LINE ONE ONLY also keeps it independent of the v2 continuation block (kogaki#28, story 1.10), whose validation stays with check-consult-receipts.sh — that check's report-never-gate contract is not absorbed, redefined or deleted, because this one gates a DIFFERENT property. It BINDS PRESENCE, NOT ORDER: a receipt written after the code it should have preceded satisfies it exactly as one written before, nothing in this repository observes that ordering, and the gap is stated rather than assumed covered (observed live on the story-1.10 branch). THE ATTRIBUTION HALF IS CARRIER-LESS AND MARKED: line one names a pin, never a boundary, so one receipt satisfies every matched boundary and a PR touching two while consulting one passes — carrier-less by omission is the defect, carrier-less with a reopen trigger is admissible (topics/knowledge-architecture.md:52@ed47fbd). FALSE POSITIVES ARE ACCEPTED AND DISCHARGED rather than narrowed away: an incidental term match is answered by the same act a real one asks for, so a spurious match costs one consultation rather than a false verdict — the map's ratified accretion polarity preserved at gate severity (owner decision at implementation; narrowing to diff paths alone was considered and declined as a silent shrink of what the map binds). THE SOURCE SET IS DECLARED and so is what it could not read — diff paths, changed text (commit messages, PR body), and the linked issue body, with an unavailable source NAMED rather than passed over, since an instrument that reports absence without establishing it is the defect check-review-report.sh refuses one layer up; an unreadable or unparseable map is COULD NOT ESTABLISH and fails, in its own wording, because a fallback worded as a finding accuses. The embedded fixture pass runs every invocation and needs no network, firing BOTH discriminating cases — matched+receipt passes, matched+none fails — plus source coverage, outcome-invariance, line-one-only, use-vs-mention, and the word-bound case that keeps short terms from matching inside longer words
admission.removal_signal: a receipt grammar that names the boundary it discharges — once a receipt carries its own boundary reference, the presence-over-the-branch approximation this check makes is the wrong carrier and is replaced by per-boundary attribution rather than widened. Fires on the reopen trigger in the file header: one PR that matched two or more boundaries, carried a receipt for only one, and shipped a defect the unconsulted boundary would have caught
admission.removal_instrument: act: the PR that lands a boundary-naming receipt grammar — its licensing issue owes per-boundary attribution and this check's replacement row in the same act

admission.contract: the review lane's presence half (specs/SPEC.md §4 PR-gate clause, kogaki#34): asserts that a review-lane report EXISTS on the pull request for its CURRENT head AND that no finding in it is declared blocking and still open — the property is CONVERGED OR ESCALATED rather than reviewed-once (kogaki#34 amendment). The head sha is part of presence rather than decoration — a report written against an earlier push reviewed code the PR no longer proposes, so it is reported STALE rather than counted (proposals-carry-the-state-they-were-computed-against applied to the reviewing act). It reads the DECLARED SEVERITY FIELD and never the findings' prose: whether a finding IS blocking is the reviewer's judgment recorded in a typed record, whether the PR CONTAINS an open blocking one is a fact over that record — the two-layer split's own test rather than an exception to it. The no-open-blocking half is CARRIER-LESS and MARKED: an empty findings record satisfies it and nothing distinguishes a thorough review from one that looked at nothing, so it carries a reopen trigger (one PR that passed with an empty record and later needed correction) rather than being carrier-less by omission, which is the defect. THREE-VALUED, with the third value EARNED BY EVIDENCE: exactly one state is CANNOT-DETERMINE — a lookup that succeeded and established there is no pull request. gh missing, a failed call, or a PR whose head will not resolve are COULD NOT ESTABLISH and fail, because a gate that exits 0 whenever its own instrument is unavailable disappears silently in the condition where it matters. The head is resolved independently of the comments fetch and an unknown head is never 'present' — both were fail-open paths reachable through the documented injection route (PR #44 review). FINDINGS BIND TO THEIR REPORT SEGMENT: only findings under a report naming the CURRENT head gate, a stale segment's findings being that round's record rather than this head's state — an unsegmented union deadlocked the rally at its first real use, since clearing a round-1 finding would have required editing the round-1 comment against clause 4's every-round-leaves-its-record (PR #44 review, round 1). States in its own output what it does NOT carry: whether the report's author differs from the work's author is unobservable, because session identity is in neither git nor GitHub metadata (measured on PR #43 — PR author, every commit author and the comment author are one login), so the isolation half is an obligation in .claude/skills/review-lane/SKILL.md and is ADVICE rather than enforcement. The embedded fixture pass runs every invocation and needs no network, because a check whose only exercise is the live path is untested wherever that path is unavailable. BLOCKING GATES ONLY WITH ITS JUSTIFICATION PRESENT (kogaki#72): a blocking finding carries [policy: <pin>] or [harm: <one line>] to gate; an unjustified blocking is downgraded to should by name, failing toward merge — presence is the fact read here, adequacy stays the lane's judgment. REPORTS AND FINDINGS COUNT ONLY FROM TRUSTED AUTHORS (kogaki#56): comments are fetched with their authors and filtered to the repository owner plus pipeline.json's merge_author_allowlist before parsing — an author-blind parse let any commenter on a public repo spoof presence with a hand-written token, or hold a PR hostage with a foreign blocking line; a dropped spoof-shaped comment is reported, never silently discarded, and the trust-assembly fixture pass discriminates both directions
admission.removal_signal: a carrier that makes the ISOLATION half observable — a harness-side record of which session authored which act, or a review transport whose identity differs from the author's by construction (a bot account, a separate app installation). Today this check enforces presence while isolation is advice; once independence is mechanically decidable, the property worth asserting changes and a presence-only check is the wrong carrier for it
admission.removal_instrument: none: session identity exists in no substrate this repository reads (measured on PR #43 — PR author, commit authors and comment author are one login); the observing carrier would be harness-side or a distinct review identity, both outside this tree

admission.contract: the event adapter's two contracts, both found broken in one held run (kogaki#65): the trigger fires ONCE PER CREATED PULL REQUEST rather than once per tool call, and it closes stdin on the sessions it spawns. The first was a re.search over the tool response — first match only — so a Bash call that created PRs #63 and #64 fired the sweep for #63 alone and #64 reached the presence gate unreviewed, with ~/.kogaki/review-trigger.log carrying no --pr 64 line at any position; the second is why both held-run reviewers reported their prompts contaminated with this repository's own driver source, reaching them through an inherited descriptor. Exercises pr_numbers() over six cases (multi-PR, single, duplicate, ordered, absent, empty) and asserts BOTH that main() routes through that function — an inlined regression would leave the fixture passing over dead code — and that the Popen closes stdin. States what it does NOT verify: that the hook is registered in .claude/settings.json, that the harness fires it, and that the spawned sweep accomplishes anything, all of which are occasions rather than logic and stay with the presence gate
admission.removal_signal: the trigger's replacement by a lane-layer invocation that fires the sweep for the PR it just created (kogaki#65 remedy 4's second half) — at that point the hook is the manual-creation fallback rather than the primary carrier, and a fixture over its extraction stops being the thing standing between a batched creation and an unreviewed PR
admission.removal_instrument: act: the PR that lands the lane-layer invocation (kogaki#65 remedy 4, second half) — its licensing issue owes this check's re-classification to manual-fallback carrier in the same act

admission.contract: the external-dependency registry (specs/SPEC.md:69-80, specs/spec-external-deps/SPEC.md; kogaki#55): the capabilities this repository NEEDS but cannot install, declared in deps/registry.json and read at run time rather than assumed. The specimen is the held run on PR #51, where three obstacles — the spawned reviewer's tool grants, the repository's allow_auto_merge, the merge deny's install state — were ONE defect, all assumed and none declared, so an unmet dependency presented as a stall or as a grant that was silently impossible to exercise. Reads specs/spec-external-deps/deps-schema.json's field lists rather than restating them, the same single-carrier arrangement check-gate-carrier.sh has against gate-schema.json. CONFORMANCE IS ITS SUBJECT AND THE WORLD IS A REPORT: it fails on a malformed or incomplete entry and never on an unmet dependency — the schema's own never_fails_on list, the same split this registry's consult-receipts entry already records ('Fails only on a malformed receipt, never on the count'), because whether a setting elsewhere is flipped changes without anyone touching the diff under review. EVERY ROW IS RENDERED, INCLUDING THE ZEROES: each decidable verification is EXECUTED and its result printed present or absent, each non-decidable entry's typed `none: <why>` is printed as its own row rather than omitted (a reason is evidence, an omission is not), and an empty registry's zero is printed through the same code path a fixture asserts, because a silent pass is indistinguishable from a check that did not run. A READ THAT DID NOT COMPLETE IS NOT AN ABSENCE: a command exiting non-zero is COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH on its own row and never 'absent', and every read runs under a hard timeout so a hanging network call cannot cost the pre-push loop unboundedly. The non-member fallback is carried rather than promised: deps/registry.json's observed_non_members list is rendered whether empty or not, and a recorded non-member stating no reason FAILS — admit-with-disclosure made checkable, which is the load-bearing half of an enumeration that can never be complete. States what it does NOT carry: nothing in this repository DETECTS that an act depended on an undeclared capability, so that list is hand-written and the observation half is carrier-less with a reopen trigger rather than carrier-less by omission; and whether a declared read answers the question its `answers` line claims, and whether an absence_signature is the signature the absence really leaves, are judgment and route to kogaki#13. The embedded fixture pass runs every invocation and needs no network: 12 entry-shape cases (conformant and malformed both fired), the four verification-read states including the two never-fails-on cases asserted by state rather than only by not-failing, duplicate ids, both directions of the non-member fallback, and the empty-registry rendering
admission.removal_signal: a host-side read of a spawned session's grant set, or any harness surface that reports the capabilities a run will actually have BEFORE it runs — at that point the needed-capability question is answered by the host rather than by a declared enumeration this repository maintains by hand, and a registry whose entries are hand-written is the wrong carrier for it. Fires the day the third entry's typed `none:` becomes decidable
admission.removal_instrument: probe: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('deps/registry.json')); e=[x for x in d['dependencies'] if x['id']=='spawned-session-tool-grants']; sys.exit(0 if e and e[0]['verification'].get('decidable') else 1)"
